items.headline: Oracle sends a force majeure notice on its 2.45-gigawatt Stargate data center in New Mexico
items.why: The notice, which protects Oracle from penalties if the facility misses its 2028 target amid a delayed pipeline and a pending air-quality permit, is an early sign that some of the AI buildout's most ambitious timelines may not hold.

sources.title: Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center

items.headline: AI memory stocks Micron and SanDisk keep rallying on a supply crunch, even with Nvidia locking in $279 billion of future orders
items.why: Both stocks still trade at a fraction of the market's average earnings multiple despite gains of roughly 270% and 700% this year, showing how far a genuine hardware shortage can re-rate a stock beyond what AI hype alone explains.

sources.title: AI memory stocks surge as SanDisk rockets 700% and Micron gains 270% in 2026

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude independently identified a previously unknown CRISPR-like enzyme system in phage DNA
items.why: Outside researchers immediately questioned whether the find has any real biological function, a reminder that a model surfacing a novel pattern is not the same as discovering a usable capability.

sources.title: Claude Found a Mysterious CRISPR-Like System—but Anthropic Can't Say What It's Capable Of

items.headline: The Federal Reserve proposes reserve and capital rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act
items.why: A 60-day comment period means the rules governing who can safely issue a dollar-backed stablecoin are still being written, keeping regulatory uncertainty alive for issuers and their bank partners.

items.headline: Bitget says hackers linked to North Korea stole $351.6 million from its hot and warm wallets
items.why: The exchange's own security team ties the attack pattern to known North Korean groups, adding to a year in which state-linked hacking has become one of crypto's largest recurring costs.

items.headline: Iran offers a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the naval blockade and sanctions relief
items.why: The offer restates terms from a June understanding rather than new demands, and Washington has called the talks only "positive and constructive" — so the standoff that has strangled Hormuz shipping is not yet resolved.

sources.title: Iran's Seven-Day Plan to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz

items.headline: A private survey shows a surprise jump in US orders for Chinese goods ahead of the Trump-Xi summit
items.why: The China Beige Book's orders gauge swinging from -12 a year ago to +13 this month, even as overall exports stay depressed, suggests companies are quietly restocking ahead of the summit rather than waiting for a resolved trade relationship.

sources.title: U.S. Orders For Chinese Goods Jumped Ahead Of Trump-Xi Summit. The Rebound Caught Researchers By Surprise.

items.why: Strong growth data is now working against risk assets rather than for them, because it feeds the same rate-hike expectations that are pressuring bonds, gold, and crypto alike.

items.headline: Gold falls to $4,265 as strong PMI data and a bond selloff outweigh Strait of Hormuz safe-haven demand
items.why: With support layered at $4,235, then $4,230 and $3,996, a further break lower would be an early sign that hawkish Fed expectations are starting to dominate gold's price action over geopolitical risk.

items.why: Oil is being pulled in two directions at once — diplomacy that could reopen Hormuz versus attacks that could disrupt a different major producer — leaving prices unusually sensitive to headlines either way.

items.headline: Copper hits a record $6.95 a pound as Shanghai warehouse stocks fall to their lowest since 2023
items.why: New mine supply takes roughly 18 years to reach production while AI data centers are pulling forward copper demand within 2-3 years, a structural mismatch that makes this rally look more durable than a typical speculative spike.

sources.title: Copper Futures Hit Record $6.95 a Pound in 2026, Outpacing Gold
